findings.summary: Answer 'does this call retain its argument' once: retainedArgumentIndex (listener second argument, browser timer first) inside callRetainsArgument, shared by the inline-arrow root and the identifier arm; the separate listener/timer arms and isStoredArgumentCallback are gone.
Resolve the retaining helper with tryResolveFunctionDeclaration; the strict resolver had made the analysis refuse a generic or rest-parameter helper reached only from erased code.
Drop the declaration-file/external-library guard: the resolver returns only declarations with bodies, so the pinned package never resolves.

Store a local function by the rule recursiveStorageEscapes applies: any reference that is not a direct callee (passed by name, assigned, pushed, returned, captured), replacing the shorthand, property, listener, timer, helper-argument and return arms.
One record-member predicate (method, get, set, property arrow on an object literal), one local-function-name helper and one storeNamed closure replace the duplicated spellings in both walks.
Walk the owner's children instead of guarding node === owner three times; a record method analysed as its own owner no longer cells its own locals.

Data-sink closures (push/unshift/add/set arguments, property or element assignment, array elements) and any callback registered inside another callback argument are roots: a pushed handler and a requestAnimationFrame callback armed from a frame callback no longer write private copies.
A named loop handed to requestAnimationFrame is a kept value like any other; the RAF exclusion covers only the inline entry-level callback, and the two application-loop tests pin the cell spelling.
Trim the comments to the contract and correct the owner-guard example, which named a shape that never reached it.
Registry entry keeps only what withDerivedPaths does not derive, and its comment states the pose arithmetic instead of repeating the scene header.

The unit test imports the example's countdown module instead of a byte-identical fixture; one entry source and one flipped-cell matcher serve the countdown tests; the vacuous constant clause becomes a timer-re-armed closure whose own local stays plain; new tests cover pushed closures and nested callbacks.

Per-identifier callee resolution in the stored-function walk is gone with the value-position rule; the remaining analysis cost measured at most 0.3% of a demo generation and the new cells (nine across eight demos) are allocated once in setup code.
Name the actual contract in the frame-callback refusal instead of onBeforeRender for every timer, interval and listener.
Derive the cell decision from the emitter's by-value capture sites, or refuse a write to a by-value capture of a mutable binding, instead of a syntactic retained set.
findings.blockedBy: Declarations are emitted before the closures that capture them, so the decision needs the typed user-code IR's escape graph or a pre-pass over the emitter's capture sites; a refusal's false-refusal rate across the registered matrix has not been measured.

findings.summary: Spell the browser timer family once across browser-erasure's deferred-call test, user-functions' directCalls (bare setTimeout text) and the setInterval lowering, which ignores window.setInterval.
findings.blockedBy: The three spellings accept different programs today (window.setInterval lowers nowhere); aligning them changes accepted timer forms and needs its own generation sweep.
